STM32 Data Logger (stm32/)¶

Decoding the STM32 data-logger .BIN format — frames delimited by 0xFF 0xFF, byte-stuffed payloads, CRC16-protected — into Packet objects and converting to/from .npz, plus the serial service and live stream viewer used to pull recordings off the device. serial (pyserial) and matplotlib are mocked at build time, so these modules render from their docstrings without those packages installed.

Binary parser¶

stm32.bin_parser.packet¶

Data model for one decoded STM32 sensor packet.

A packet holds one sensor’s samples for a single timestamp. The STM32 groups samples into chunks identified by a small integer id; CHUNK_NAMES maps those ids to human-readable sensor names.

AutoDNA.stm32.bin_parser.packet.CHUNK_NAMES = {1: 'gyro', 2: 'accel', 3: 'mag'}¶

Maps a chunk id (from the binary stream) to its sensor name.

stm32.bin_parser.stm_utils¶

Decode the STM32 data-logger binary format into Packet objects.

Wire format: packets are framed by 0xFF 0xFF; the payload is byte-stuffed (0xFE escape) and protected by a trailing CRC16 (Modbus, poly 0xA001). Each payload carries a 32-bit millisecond timestamp and one or more sensor chunks of int16 XYZ samples. This module parses that format and converts to/from .npz for downstream processing.

AutoDNA.stm32.bin_parser.stm_utils.unstuff_bytes(data)[source]¶

Reverse the 0xFE byte-stuffing.

Each 0xFE marks an escaped byte; the following byte is XORed with 0xFE to recover the original. Raises ValueError if the data ends on a dangling escape.

Parameters:

data (bytes)

Return type:

bytes

stm32.bin_parser.parser¶

Command-line tool to decode STM32 .BIN recordings into .npz.

Handles a single .bin file or a whole folder of them. Run with:

python -m AutoDNA.stm32.bin_parser.parser <input.bin | input_dir> [-o out] [--preview]

stm32.stream¶

Live serial viewer for the STM32 logger.

Reads the raw byte stream from the device on PORT, saves it to sensor.bin, decodes 0xFF 0xFF-delimited packets on the fly, and animates a rolling 5-second window of gyro/accel/mag samples with matplotlib.

AutoDNA.stm32.stream.graphing()[source]¶

Build the figure, start the serial-reader thread, and run the live animation.
